items.hook: A series of bombings in Baghdad, Iraq, kills 101 and injures 565 others.
items.body: The August 2009 Baghdad bombings were three coordinated car bomb attacks and a number of mortar strikes in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, on 19 August 2009. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: An Imperial army under Ludwig of Baden defeats the Ottomans in the battle of Slankamen.
items.body: Louis William, Margrave of Baden-Baden was the ruling Margrave of Baden-Baden in Germany, chief commander of the Imperial army and Reichsgeneralfeldmarschall of the Holy Roman Empire. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Hungerford massacre: In the United Kingdom, Michael Ryan kills sixteen people with a semi-automatic rifle and then commits suicide.
items.body: The Hungerford massacre was a spree shooting in Wiltshire and Berkshire, England, which occurred on 19 August 1987 when 27-year-old Michael Ryan shot and killed sixteen people, including his mother and an unarmed police officer, before killing himself. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The Tambov Rebellion breaks out, in response to the Bolshevik policy of Prodrazvyorstka.
items.body: The Tambov Rebellion of 1920–1922 was one of the largest and best-organized peasant rebellions challenging the Bolshevik government during the Russian Civil War. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Dakota War: During an uprising in Minnesota, Lakota warriors decide not to attack heavily defended Fort Ridgely and instead turn to the settlement of New Ulm, killing white settlers along the way.
items.body: The Dakota War of 1862, also known as the U.S.-Dakota War of 1862, the Sioux Uprising, the Dakota Uprising, the Sioux Outbreak of 1862, the Dakota Conflict, or Little Crow's War, was an armed conflict between the United States and several eastern bands of Dakota collectively known as the Santee Sioux. One of those things you can't un-know.
